summary: The note outlines how high school athletes can navigate college recruitment, covering the NCAA/NAIA timeline, balancing academics and athletics, personal branding, communicating with coaches, eligibility registration and scholarships, and support systems. It cites quotes from coaches and experts and local examples and events from late 2023 to spring 2024. It concludes that early preparation, strategy and communication are essential.
one_line: A guide for aspiring college athletes on recruitment timelines, academics, self-promotion, coach communication, eligibility registration, scholarships and support networks.
key_facts: Recruitment can begin as early as freshman year of high school for some sports.

Jack Thompson, a former university recruiter, says Division I football recruits can receive non-recruiting materials beginning September 1 of their sophomore year, but direct contact only after their junior year.
As of September 1, 2023, changes in NCAA recruitment guidelines took effect, with more emphasis on the junior year for official visits and substantive coach interactions.
Sarah Menendez, a high school soccer coach in Texas, stresses that colleges want athletes who succeed in the classroom as well as on the field.
A College Prep seminar was held on October 15, 2023, in Austin, Texas, to help student-athletes balance academics with competition.
Marcus Johnson, a local high school basketball player, updated his stats and game footage online, attracted Division II and III schools, and received multiple college camp offers in February 2024.
Kevin Robbins, a communications expert and consultant for young athletes, advises athletes to be proactive: "Don't wait for coaches to find you."
The Annual College Athletic Conference was held on November 5, 2023, in Florida, letting athletes meet college representatives, coaches and current college athletes.
Registering with the NCAA Eligibility Center and NAIA Eligibility Center is essential; without it athletes cannot make official visits or receive scholarships from Division I and II schools.
On December 8, 2023, the NCAA hosted a virtual workshop on the registration process and securing athletic scholarships.
Only a fraction of high school athletes receive scholarships, so both academic and athletic performance matter.
Emily Watson, a volleyball player from Colorado, credited family support and her high school coach for securing a spot in a competitive volleyball program in spring 2024.
The Colorado Springs Volleyball Club launched a mentorship program on January 12, 2024, pairing aspiring college athletes with former collegiate players.
